text.p: Leaders Juventus crashed to an astonishing 3-0 home defeat to 10-man Udinese on Sunday.
The upset allowed Parma, 1-0 winners at Roma, to cut the European Cup holders' Italian championship lead to three points.
It was Juve's third league defeat of the season and their first in 16 league and cup matches.
It was also their first in Turin since losing to Sampdoria by the same score exactly a year ago.
To add to the disbelief a week after their own 6-1 humiliation of AC Milan, Italy international Christian Vieri and France's Zinedine Zidane both missed second-half penalties.
Brazilian Marcio Amoroso struck twice and Germany's Oliver Bierhoff added a third as Udinese made light of the third minute dismissal of their Belgian defender Regis Genaux.
Udinese scored all their goals before the 59th minute dismissal of Juventus midfielder Alessio Tacchinardi.
Parma took full advantage of Juve's reverse to win courtesy of a goal from Argentine Hernan Crespo.
